Copy a paywall's current design into a new paywall of the same project, to try a variation without
touching the original. The copy is made for the same locations and uses the same images, fonts,
components and products. It has no builds and no location shows it, so nobody sees it until it is
deployed and shown. It is named after the paywall with "copy" and a free slug unless --name and
--slug say otherwise.

Usage:
  voidhash paywall duplicate [paywall] [flags]

Arguments:
  paywall  The paywall's slug, name or id

Flags:
  -h, --help               Show help for this command
      --json               Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --name <name>        The copy's name (default: the paywall's name followed by "copy")
      --project <project>  Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default: this
                           directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet              Print only ids, one per line
      --slug <slug>        The copy's slug, which cannot change later (default: the paywall's slug
                           followed by -copy)

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash paywall duplicate summer-sale
  voidhash paywall duplicate summer-sale --name "Summer sale B" --slug summer-sale-b
